Only with `--dry-run`. Let me check that the script still supports it.

8:    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
10:    bucket = os.environ.get("EXPORT_BUCKET", "ledgerline-exports-dev")
11:    print(f"exporting {args.env} to {bucket} (dry_run={args.dry_run})")

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`.

An EngramDB hazard memory says that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A real run against staging would write to prod.

The script still has the `--dry-run` flag (`scripts/export.py:8`). It reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` from the environment (line 10) and prints the bucket it would use. The excerpt I read doesn't show what `--dry-run` actually skips, so I haven't confirmed that it avoids writing. Read the rest of the script before you rely on it.

Something like this should be safe:

```
python scripts/export.py <staging-env-arg> --dry-run
```

I haven't run it. Check the printed bucket line first. If you want a real (non-dry) test, point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a non-prod bucket explicitly.
